sample_unit: stimuli (EU-Emotion Stimulus Set body language items)

links.outcome: Effect of chain-of-thought prompting on emotion recognition across models
links.effect: CoT significantly enhanced Gemini Pro 2.0 (OR = 3.97, p < .001) but significantly impaired Gemini Flash 2.0 (OR = 0.40, p < .001), creating a blind spot for negative emotions.
links.quote: Interaction analyses revealed divergent effects: CoT prompting significantly enhanced Gemini Pro 2.0 (OR = 3.97, p < .001) and mitigated its “positivity bias,” whereas it significantly impaired Gemini Flash 2.0 (OR = 0.40, p < .001), creating a specific blind spot for negative emotions.

links.outcome: Emotion recognition performance of Gemini models versus human benchmark on body-language stimuli
links.effect: Gemini Pro 2.0 CCR = 0.722, on par with human benchmark (0.717); FlashThinking CCR = 0.463, failing to outperform generalist models.
links.quote: Instead, the high-capacity generalist model (Gemini Pro 2.0) exhibited the highest performance (CCR = 0.722, 95% CI [0.590, 0.838]), significantly outperforming all other models (OR ≤ 0.19, p < .001) and achieving parity with human benchmarks (CCR = 0.717).

unlisted_practices: Model-capacity-dependent selection of chain-of-thought prompting for emotion recognition
Specialized reasoning architectures versus generalist models for non-verbal emotion recognition

screen.reason: Empirically assesses how chain-of-thought prompting impacts multimodal emotion recognition across different model architectures for mental health applications.
